item.text: I’ll apply the lean-run skill to a read-only assessment: compare the contract and baseline with the candidate, inspect the added tests, and run checks using temporary paths.

---
name: lean-run
description: Own an end-to-end implementation request from initial decisions to verified delivery, coordinating available Lean skills without repeated planning or manual handoffs.
license: MIT
---

# lean-run

Carry the request through its authorized endpoint. Follow project instructions, preserve unrelated work and reuse verified context. This skill works alone; companions are optional and no Lean runtime or workflow directory is required.

## Settle scope, then act

Read applicable instructions and the nearest relevant source/tests in one focused pass. Record outcome, observable acceptance, constraints, verification and destination; a sentence suffices for a bounded change. Use standard procedure depth unless requested otherwise; depth does not select model settings. For broad ambiguity read [exploration](references/exploration.md); skip discovery loops for clear requests or an instruction to proceed. Ask only indispensable missing decisions and continue independent work. Silence is not consent.

Resolve consequential business rules, permissions, data lifecycle and external contracts before implementation. Decide reversible details from project conventions. Implementation authorization includes matching preparation and verification without another plan approval. Requested PRs/deployments remain acceptance and require matching authority/tools; finish preparation before any necessary final approval. End-to-end work grants no extra publishing, spending or provider permissions. Create workflow files only when requested. On pause, handoff or cross-session resume read [continuation](references/handoff.md).

## Use the smallest complete procedure

Reuse or classify risk as LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH and quality as STANDARD/HIGH/VERY_HIGH. Consequential security, destructive data and breaking external contracts are HIGH risk. For persistent, concurrent or access-scoped **application data** writes, use [write integrity](references/write-integrity.md) to select and verify one mechanism before expanding implementation or review.

For a bounded implementation, turn the public signatures and contract into a short requirement-to-evidence map before editing. Include container element/key types, copy ownership, failure atomicity and replay when specified. Use one targeted batch for reproduction; reuse it to verify the edit. Write compact checks for gaps and use test-first development when requested. Expand investigation for a demonstrated failure or unresolved requirement.

After the edit, run affected and required checks on final content, exercise the relevant public journey with important failures, and review the complete diff including new files. Reuse passing evidence whose inputs and relevant environment remain unchanged. Do not repeat whole suites to confirm a clear completion summary. A check proves only its mapped acceptance; unit tests, builds and mocks do not establish an untested live integration. Record actions, environment, expected/observed results and simulated boundaries. Disclose unavailable reproduction or live access and report remaining acceptance.

Batch the contract, instructions and named source/test reads. Use VCS diffs when available; in a standalone fixture, save one temporary copy before editing and compare directly. Inspect added files separately. Keep source on disk; reread only changed or relevant sections. Serialize dependent work.

For **assessment-only** work, inspect contract, current source/diff and tests; run required checks once, then independently probe remaining boundary/failure risks through the public interface. Do not recreate a comprehensive suite or alternative implementation when inspected source and verified tests establish the behavior. Expand for a concrete gap or contradiction. Reproduce old failures only to establish a finding or when requested. Assessment does not authorize implementation or delivery.

## Review and repair

LOW permits an acceptance self-check; MEDIUM needs focused correctness/regression review; HIGH needs a fresh independent reviewer. Quality HIGH requires at least MEDIUM review; VERY_HIGH requires HIGH. A reviewer inspects current source and runs independent checks; author conclusions cannot supply independence. Unavailable required independence is BLOCKED.

Derive equivalence classes and boundary/failure cases from acceptance. Extend to exhaustive/random sweeps only for an identified gap or hypothesis; case count alone is not evidence. Repair demonstrated in-scope failures, rerun affected checks and renew review of changed content. Verify integrated worker results. Stop once mandatory coverage and findings are resolved.

Count review REWORK across the entire task, companions, workers and resumes. After the second REWORK, allow one final fix-only pass plus verification/review; unresolved mandatory findings mean FAILED. Never reset counts through nested workflows. Each repair needs new evidence/hypothesis and a distinguishing check; abandon approaches yielding no new information. Suspected flaky checks permit at most two disclosed unchanged retries. Never weaken acceptance, disable checks or omit mandatory work for speed. Separate unrelated failures and seek direction only if repairing them expands scope.

## Load procedures only when useful

Read an available companion only when its procedure helps the remaining work; pass settled scope and relevant raw evidence. If absent, perform the core procedure here. Missing a skill is not a blocker; a required capability can be.

| Need | Optional companion |
| --- | --- |
| Repository, conventions, agent instructions | `lean-target`, `lean-init`, `lean-instructions` |
| Scope, decisions, research | `lean-scope`, `lean-grill`, `lean-research` |
| Implementation, useful delegation | `lean-task`, `lean-agents` |
| Review, completion evidence | `lean-review`, `lean-gate` |
| Security, authorized release/recovery | `lean-security`, `lean-release` |
| Requested depth or skill/model update | `lean-effort`, `lean-update`, `lean-model-update` |

This workflow requests selective delegation when useful or required for independence, subject to host/user restrictions. Keep small work inline; default to one active worker, with more only for explicit parallel work. Before dispatch read [delegation](references/delegation.md). One controller owns scope, integration, repair counts and delivery.

For noisy suites or expected failures, execute the bundled [check runner](scripts/check.py): `python3 /resolved/skill/path/scripts/check.py -- COMMAND ARG...`. It retains full stdout/stderr, returns the command exit status and emits a bounded excerpt. No default timeout; optional `--timeout SECONDS`; `--log NEW_PATH` refuses overwrite. Execute it without reading its implementation unless debugging/changing it. Small bounded checks can run directly. If Python is unavailable, use equivalent host capture without installing a runtime. Inspect saved logs for failures or ambiguous completion until distinct causes are understood; keep full logs accessible and never hide failures.

## Deliver with evidence

For user-facing work include affected accessibility, keyboard/focus, screen sizes and loading/empty/error/recovery states. Performance work needs a representative workload and measured baseline before optimization; a proposal alone does not authorize benchmarking. Security work maps protected data, entry points, trust transitions and permissions, then probes relevant abuse cases. Releases check artifact/environment, dependencies/configuration/migration compatibility, health criteria and authorized recovery before mutation; verify deployment and observation. Inspect uncertain state before retrying. Application rollback grants no destructive data-restore authority; a failed release followed by recovery remains a failed release.

Advance when evidence is sufficient and reopen decisions only for new requirements or contradictions. Match every acceptance item, including delivery, to current commands/actions and outcomes, review coverage and limits. DONE requires all mandatory acceptance, verification, review and the authorized destination. Otherwise report BLOCKED or FAILED, completed work, affected acceptance and the exact next action. A plan, worker report or stage PASS does not complete unfinished work. Keep updates/final concise; do not ask to continue authorized work. These procedures are not enforced hooks or a guarantee of success.

This is an isolated LOCAL benchmark fixture. Use Python standard library only. Work exclusively in this workspace; do not inspect evaluator scripts, sibling trials, global skills, other repositories, credentials, network or external services. Read .agents/skills/lean-run/SKILL.md and apply it. Do not modify CONTRACT.md, AGENTS.md, supplied test_public.py or .agents. You may edit application Python and add meaningful tests. Use python3 -B -m unittest discover -v and real public interfaces. No installs, commits, pushes, publication or extra agents. The coordinator supplies fresh independent review after implementation. When that review is mandatory, explicitly report it pending; do not claim it occurred. Deliver local code and a concise evidence report in the final response. Do not create workflow files. These read boundaries are instructional, not OS sandboxing.
Repair ledger.py. Public API: Ledger(balances: dict[str,int]),
transfer(source,target,amount,key), batch(operations). Preserve the
public balances and history dictionaries and existing valid behavior.
Constructor copies input; nonnegative integer balances, excluding
bool, are required. Transfers require distinct existing accounts,
amount a positive int excluding bool, and a nonempty string key.
Reject invalid values, unavailable accounts and insufficient funds
with ValueError and absolutely no state change. Return a receipt
{'source':source,'target':target,'amount':amount,'key':key}.
A replay of a successful key with the same payload returns an equal
receipt with no second mutation; a changed payload is a ValueError.
Returned receipts must not let callers mutate internal history.
batch accepts a list of operation dictionaries using these names,
returning receipts in order. A batch is atomic: on any failure both
balances/history equal their pre-batch state, including earlier valid
operations; successful batches preserve ordinary replay semantics.
No persistence, concurrency or external service is requested here.
Add meaningful tests and exercise an integrated multi-transfer flow.

1	class Ledger:
     2	    """An in-memory ledger with idempotent transfers and atomic batches."""
     3	
     4	    def __init__(self, balances):
     5	        if not isinstance(balances, dict):
     6	            raise ValueError("balances must be a dictionary")
     7	        for account, balance in balances.items():
     8	            if not isinstance(account, str):
     9	                raise ValueError("account names must be strings")
    10	            if (not isinstance(balance, int) or isinstance(balance, bool)
    11	                    or balance < 0):
    12	                raise ValueError("balances must be nonnegative integers")
    13	        self.balances = dict(balances)
    14	        self.history = {}
    15	
    16	    def transfer(self, source, target, amount, key):
    17	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not isinstance(target, str):
    18	            raise ValueError("account names must be strings")
    19	        if source == target:
    20	            raise ValueError("source and target must be distinct")
    21	        if source not in self.balances or target not in self.balances:
    22	            raise ValueError("source and target must exist")
    23	        if not isinstance(amount, int) or isinstance(amount, bool) or amount <= 0:
    24	            raise ValueError("amount must be a positive integer")
    25	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
    26	            raise ValueError("key must be a nonempty string")
    27	
    28	        receipt = dict(source=source, target=target, amount=amount, key=key)
    29	        if key in self.history:
    30	            if self.history[key] != receipt:
    31	                raise ValueError("key already used for a different transfer")
    32	            return self.history[key].copy()
    33	        if self.balances[source] < amount:
    34	            raise ValueError("insufficient funds")
    35	
    36	        self.balances[source] -= amount
    37	        self.balances[target] += amount
    38	        self.history[key] = receipt
    39	        return receipt.copy()
    40	
    41	    def batch(self, operations):
    42	        if not isinstance(operations, list):
    43	            raise ValueError("operations must be a list")
    44	
    45	        # Only commit once every operation succeeds. Stored receipts are never
    46	        # edited, so sharing them with the staged history is safe.
    47	        staged = Ledger(self.balances)
    48	        staged.history = self.history.copy()
    49	        receipts = []
    50	        fields = {"source", "target", "amount", "key"}
    51	        for operation in operations:
    52	            if not isinstance(operation, dict) or set(operation) != fields:
    53	                raise ValueError("each operation must contain source, target, amount and key")
    54	            receipts.append(staged.transfer(**operation))
    55	
    56	        # Preserve references held by callers to both public dictionaries.
    57	        self.balances.update(staged.balances)
    58	        self.history.update(staged.history)
    59	        return receipts

import copy
import unittest

from ledger import Ledger


def operation(source="a", target="b", amount=10, key="new"):
    return {"source": source, "target": target, "amount": amount, "key": key}


class LedgerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ledger = Ledger({"a": 100, "b": 30, "c": 0})

    def assert_rejected_without_change(self, action):
        balances = self.ledger.balances
        history = self.ledger.history
        before = copy.deepcopy((balances, history))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            action()
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.history, history)
        self.assertEqual((balances, history), before)

    def test_constructor_copies_input(self):
        balances = {"a": 100, "b": 0}
        ledger = Ledger(balances)
        balances["a"] = 5
        balances["outside"] = 10
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {"a": 100, "b": 0})
        ledger.transfer("a", "b", 20, "one")
        self.assertEqual(balances, {"a": 5, "b": 0, "outside": 10})

    def test_constructor_rejects_boolean_balance(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            Ledger({"a": True})

    def test_constructor_rejects_invalid_containers_keys_and_balances(self):
        invalid = [None, [], (), [("a", 10)]]
        invalid.extend({"a": 10, "b": value}
                       for value in [-1, False, 1.0, "1", None, [], {}])
        invalid.extend({key: 10} for key in [1, True, None, ("a",), b"a"])
        for balances in invalid:
            with self.subTest(balances=balances):
                before = copy.deepcopy(balances)
                with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                    Ledger(balances)
                self.assertEqual(balances, before)

    def test_empty_ledger_and_valid_balance_boundaries(self):
        empty = Ledger({})
        self.assertEqual(empty.balances, {})
        self.assertEqual(empty.history, {})
        self.assertEqual(empty.batch([]), [])

        # Account names may be any strings; a key need only be nonempty.
        large = 10 ** 100
        ledger = Ledger({"": 0, "\u0394": large})
        expected = operation("\u0394", "", large, " ")
        self.assertEqual(ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(ledger.balances, {"": large, "\u0394": 0})

    def test_transfer_preserves_public_dictionaries_and_unrelated_accounts(self):
        balances = self.ledger.balances
        history = self.ledger.history
        expected = operation(amount=100, key="full-balance")
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.history, history)
        self.assertEqual(balances, {"a": 0, "b": 130, "c": 0})
        self.assertEqual(history, {"full-balance": expected})

    def test_transfer_rejects_insufficient_funds_atomically(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "c", 5, "existing")
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 96, "too-much")
        )

    def test_transfer_rejects_boolean_amount(self):
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", True, "boolean")
        )

    def test_transfer_rejects_invalid_amounts(self):
        for amount in [False, 0, -1, 1.0, 2.5, "1", None, [], {}]:
            with self.subTest(amount=amount):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", amount, "invalid")
                )

    def test_transfer_rejects_invalid_keys(self):
        for key in ["", None, 1, True, b"key", [], {}, ("key",)]:
            with self.subTest(key=key):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 10, key)
                )

    def test_transfer_rejects_invalid_or_unavailable_accounts(self):
        for field in ["source", "target"]:
            for account in ["missing", None, 1, True, [], {}, b"a", ("a",)]:
                with self.subTest(field=field, account=account):
                    payload = operation()
                    payload[field] = account
                    self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                        lambda: self.ledger.transfer(**payload)
                    )
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "a", 10, "same-account")
        )

    def test_failed_transfer_does_not_reserve_key(self):
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 101, "retry")
        )
        expected = operation(amount=100, key="retry")
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.balances, {"a": 0, "b": 130, "c": 0})
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history, {"retry": expected})

    def test_replay_after_source_is_empty(self):
        receipt = self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 100, "all")
        before = copy.deepcopy((self.ledger.balances, self.ledger.history))
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 100, "all"), receipt)
        self.assertEqual((self.ledger.balances, self.ledger.history), before)

    def test_replay_rejects_changed_payload(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "c", 20, "seed")
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 10, "used")
        for change in [{"source": "c"}, {"target": "c"}, {"amount": 11}]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                payload = operation(key="used")
                payload.update(change)
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.transfer(**payload)
                )

    def test_replay_does_not_bypass_amount_type_validation(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 1, "one")
        for amount in [True, 1.0]:
            with self.subTest(amount=amount):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", amount, "one")
                )

    def test_same_payload_with_new_key_transfers_again(self):
        first = operation(key="first")
        second = operation(key="second")
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**first), first)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**second), second)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.balances, {"a": 80, "b": 50, "c": 0})
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history, {"first": first, "second": second})

    def test_transfer_receipt_cannot_change_history(self):
        expected = operation(key="receipt")
        receipt = self.ledger.transfer(**expected)
        receipt["amount"] = 999
        receipt["extra"] = "caller data"
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history, {"receipt": expected})
        replay = self.ledger.transfer(**expected)
        self.assertEqual(replay, expected)
        replay.clear()
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history, {"receipt": expected})

    def test_batch_rolls_back_late_failure(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "c", 5, "existing")
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.batch([
                operation(amount=20, key="first"),
                operation("b", "c", 1000, "second"),
            ])
        )

    def test_batch_rejects_malformed_operation_atomically(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "c", 5, "existing")
        malformed = [None, [], (), "operation", {},
                     {**operation(), "unexpected": 0},
                     {**operation(), 0: "extra"}]
        for missing_field in ["source", "target", "amount", "key"]:
            payload = operation()
            del payload[missing_field]
            malformed.append(payload)
        for payload in malformed:
            with self.subTest(payload=payload):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.batch([operation(), payload])
                )

    def test_batch_rejects_invalid_containers(self):
        for operations in [None, {}, (), (operation(),), "operations",
                           iter([operation()])]:
            with self.subTest(operations=operations):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.batch(operations)
                )

    def test_batch_rejects_invalid_payloads_atomically(self):
        for change in [{"amount": True}, {"target": "missing"},
                       {"source": []}, {"key": []}, {"source": "b"}]:
            with self.subTest(change=change):
                payload = operation(key="second")
                payload.update(change)
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.batch([operation(key="first"), payload])
                )

    def test_empty_batch_is_noop(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 10, "existing")
        balances = self.ledger.balances
        history = self.ledger.history
        before = copy.deepcopy((balances, history))
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch([]), [])
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.history, history)
        self.assertEqual((balances, history), before)

    def test_batch_success_obeys_order_and_preserves_input(self):
        balances = self.ledger.balances
        history = self.ledger.history
        operations = [operation("a", "c", 40, "first"),
                      operation("c", "b", 30, "second"),
                      operation("b", "a", 20, "third")]
        before = copy.deepcopy(operations)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(operations), before)
        self.assertEqual(operations, before)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.history, history)
        self.assertEqual(balances, {"a": 80, "b": 40, "c": 10})
        self.assertEqual(history, {op["key"]: op for op in before})

    def test_batch_replays_within_and_across_batches(self):
        existing = operation(amount=20, key="existing")
        self.ledger.transfer(**existing)
        onward = operation("b", "c", 50, "onward")
        returned = operation("c", "a", 10, "returned")
        operations = [existing, onward, onward, returned]
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(operations), operations)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.balances, {"a": 90, "b": 0, "c": 40})
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history,
                         {op["key"]: op for op in [existing, onward, returned]})
        before = copy.deepcopy((self.ledger.balances, self.ledger.history))
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(operations), operations)
        self.assertEqual((self.ledger.balances, self.ledger.history), before)

    def test_batch_receipts_are_detached_from_inputs_and_each_other(self):
        payload = operation()
        expected = payload.copy()
        receipts = self.ledger.batch([payload, payload])
        self.assertEqual(receipts, [expected, expected])
        payload["amount"] = 999
        receipts[0].clear()
        self.assertEqual(receipts[1], expected)
        receipts[1]["target"] = "c"
        receipts.clear()
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.history, {"new": expected})
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**expected), expected)
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.balances, {"a": 90, "b": 40, "c": 0})

    def test_batch_conflicts_with_new_or_existing_key_abort_all_changes(self):
        self.ledger.transfer("a", "b", 10, "existing")
        for conflicting in [operation(target="c", key="existing"),
                            operation(amount=11, key="fresh")]:
            with self.subTest(conflicting=conflicting):
                self.assert_rejected_without_change(
                    lambda: self.ledger.batch([operation(key="fresh"), conflicting])
                )

    def test_batch_cannot_spend_future_funds(self):
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.batch([
                operation("c", "b", 1, "too-early"),
                operation("a", "c", 1, "later"),
            ])
        )

    def test_integrated_payments_rollback_retry_and_replay(self):
        initial = {"pool": 250, "alice": 0, "bob": 0, "reserve": 50}
        self.ledger = Ledger(initial)
        balances = self.ledger.balances
        history = self.ledger.history
        opening = operation("pool", "alice", 100, "opening")
        payment = operation("alice", "bob", 40, "payment")
        fee = operation("bob", "reserve", 15, "fee")
        top_up = operation("pool", "bob", 50, "top-up")
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**opening), opening)
        payments = [opening, payment, fee, payment, top_up]
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(payments), payments)
        self.assertEqual(balances,
                         {"pool": 100, "alice": 60, "bob": 75, "reserve": 65})

        rebate = operation("reserve", "alice", 20, "rebate")
        too_large = operation("alice", "pool", 100, "refund")
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.batch([rebate, too_large])
        )
        refund = operation("alice", "pool", 80, "refund")
        recovered = [rebate, refund]
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(recovered), recovered)
        self.assertEqual(balances,
                         {"pool": 180, "alice": 0, "bob": 75, "reserve": 45})
        before = copy.deepcopy((balances, history))
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.batch(recovered), recovered)
        self.assertEqual((balances, history), before)

        final_payment = operation("bob", "alice", 5, "final")
        conflict = operation("pool", "alice", 101, "opening")
        self.assert_rejected_without_change(
            lambda: self.ledger.batch([final_payment, conflict])
        )
        self.assertEqual(self.ledger.transfer(**final_payment), final_payment)
        self.assertEqual(balances,
                         {"pool": 180, "alice": 5, "bob": 70, "reserve": 45})
        self.assertEqual(sum(balances.values()), 300)
        self.assertEqual(initial,
                         {"pool": 250, "alice": 0, "bob": 0, "reserve": 50})
        committed = [opening, payment, fee, top_up, rebate, refund, final_payment]
        self.assertEqual(history, {op["key"]: op for op in committed})
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.balances, balances)
        self.assertIs(self.ledger.history, history)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
